Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) clearly localizes the mass to the posterior mediastinum (paravertebral region), which is the most common location for neurogenic tumors like neuroblastoma in children. While lymphomas and thymomas typically present in the anterior or middle mediastinum, a well-marginated posterior mass in a 10-year-old with constitutional symptoms is most characteristic of a neuroblastic tumor.
